To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) sensory-motor areas are involved in processing of action verbs, (2) this involvement is modulated by the abstractness of the sentence, and (3) this involvement is further modulated by the degree to which the sentence is conventionalized. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sensory-motor areas are involved in conceptual processing in general, but the extent of their involvement depends on the abstractness of the meaning and the conventionalization of the expression.

the sensory-motor system is recruited for processing action idioms and action metaphors, while the recruitment of the sensory-motor systems for processing idioms is weaker and for processing metaphors stronger than for processing literal action sentences.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensory-motor regions are modulated by context and task demands, and this modulation is gradual.
action idioms are processed in a way that is distinct from literal action sentences as well as from metaphoric sentences.
